question: Should proven requester consumption make a descendant terminally `delivered` even when the requester's final outward send later fails?
rationale: The choice determines whether internal orchestration consumption or user-visible outward delivery is the terminal lifecycle boundary; source and tests can prove mechanics but cannot choose that product contract.

options.title: Accept consumption as delivery
options.body: Document the invariant and merge after exact-head persisted-state proof confirms only explicitly consumed descendants stop retrying.

options.title: Add a distinct consumed state
options.body: Record requester consumption separately from visible delivery and update cleanup and retry projections to interpret that state explicitly.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox work
options.body: Pause this PR and resolve the case with the broader durable completion inbox design tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67777.

recommendation.title: Accept consumption as delivery
recommendation.body: Document the invariant and merge after exact-head persisted-state proof confirms only explicitly consumed descendants stop retrying.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged descendant-gating work is the clearest feature-history ownership signal for the delivery invariant being extended.
